environment.description: Same Rails application deployed behind Cloudflare with the following configuration: Cloudflare Access policy requiring valid mTLS client certificate (service token) for /graphql path with certificate pinning to internal CA; Page Rule enforcing Browser Integrity Check on all asset paths; Transform Rule rewriting Content-Security-Policy response header to include 'require-sri-for script style' directive and 'script-src' restricted to 'self' with specific sha384 hashes matching deployed bundle checksums. Additionally, a Cloudflare WAF custom rule (expression: http.request.body contains "'" and http.request.uri.path eq "/graphql") set to action LOG only — note this rule does NOT block, it only logs. The actual SQL injection protection relies on the mTLS requirement which restricts access to authenticated internal services that use a parameterized GraphQL client library (graphql-client v0.18 with strict variable typing that rejects string interpolation in variable values containing SQL metacharacters via custom serializer).
